title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 3 November 2026
headline: Madras HC Grants Relief to DMK Leader, CM Vijay Distributes Rs 3,000 Crore to Self-Help Groups

top_developments.headline: Madras High Court Grants Bail to DMK Leader in CM Abuse Case
top_developments.summary: The Madras High Court has granted bail to a DMK councillor who was booked for making offensive remarks against Chief Minister Vijay. While delivering the order, the court strongly observed that police forces serve the state and the rule of law rather than any ruling political party. The ruling comes amid heightened political friction between the ruling party and the opposition across various districts in Tamil Nadu.
top_developments.why_it_matters: Reinforces judicial oversight on police actions and provides temporary legal relief to the opposition DMK amid rising political tensions.

sources.title: Madras High Court grants bail to DMK leader in CM abuse case: ‘Cops serve state, not party’

top_developments.headline: CM Vijay Distributes Rs 3,000 Crore to Women Self-Help Groups in Erode
top_developments.summary: Chief Minister Vijay distributed bank linkage funds totaling Rs 3,000 crore to 26,000 women self-help groups during a public event held at Perundurai in Erode district. During his transit, the Chief Minister also met with the Athikadavu Avinasi Project Protest Committee to discuss demands for immediate initiation of the project's second phase. The outreach program faced instant pushback from opposition leaders.
top_developments.why_it_matters: Highlights the government's direct grassroots welfare outreach ahead of upcoming regional by-elections.

sources.title: Chief Minister Vijay congratulated 26,000 women self-help groups by handing over checks for a total fund of Rs 3,000 crore.

sections.government_and_administration:
- **Asset Hoarding Case Acquittal:** A Thoothukudi court has acquitted former minister and DMK MLA Anitha Radhakrishnan, along with his family members, in a disproportionate assets case spanning nearly 20 years. ([Polimer News](https://www.polimernews.com/politicsnews/anitha-radhakrishnan-discharge-2-08-crore-disproportionate-assets-case-12779665))
- **Return of Early Screenings:** The Tamil Nadu government officially rolled back restrictions to permit early 6 am theatrical screenings for Tamil feature films across the state. ([India Today](https://news.google.?oc=5))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition:
- **EPS Slams Government on Price Rise:** AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami criticized the state administration, alleging that commodity prices have skyrocketed while GST revenue growth has slowed down. He further accused Chief Minister Vijay of selectively targeting welfare schemes toward upcoming by-election constituencies. ([Polimer News](https://www.polimernews.com/justnownews/eps-criticises-vijay-government-price-rise-gst-revenue-12778452))
- **VCK Attacks Seeman:** VCK Minister Vanni Arasu launched a scathing attack on Naam Tamilar Katchi leader Seeman, accusing him of abandoning Tamil nationalist ideology to contest an assembly by-election after Seeman remarked he would not reject 'Dravidian biryani' support. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/seeman-stands-with-hands-and-plate-out-for-dravidian-briyani-says-vck-minister-vanni-arasu))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy:
- **Madras HC Questions Police Action:** The Madras High Court raised serious questions regarding police procedures after MIDS associate professor and economist A Kalaiyarasan was picked up from his home at dawn over social media posts made from a fake account. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/madras-hc-questions-police-action-over-kalaiyarasans-detention))
- **DMDK Withdraws Plea:** The Madras High Court permitted DMDK youth wing secretary V. Vijaya Prabhakaran to formally withdraw his 2024 election petition challenging the victory of TNCC president B. Manickam Tagore in the Virudhunagar Lok Sabha constituency. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/madras-high-court-permits-dmdk-leader-vijaya-prabhakaran-to-withdraw-election-petition-against-manickam-tagore/article71660240.ece))
sections.district_developments: - **DVAC Inquiry Demanded in Chennai:** The DMK legal wing lodged a formal complaint with the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption, seeking an FIR into School Education Minister A. Rajmohan's claim that he was offered a Rs 5 crore bribe for a government board appointment. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/dmk-seeks-dvac-inquiry-into-minister-rajmohans-allegation-of-being-offered-bribery-for-post/article71656918.ece))
